one_month_reasoning: The window contains Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-15 after the close (call 5pm EDT). Q3 realized prices will be below Q2: LME 3M aluminium slid from ~$3,360/t (Sep 10) to $3,213.5/t (Sep 29), the Midwest premium eased to ~$2,403/t from its June record, and FOB WA alumina is ~$349-369/t (near cash cost for weaker refineries); management guided only ~$10M sequential alumina improvement. So Q3 EBITDA will likely step down from Q2's $901M; much of this looks priced after a ~16% fall in September (50 -> 42), and Q2 itself missed (2.12 vs 2.25-2.32). Other in-window items: China post-Golden Week restocking, an October Fed decision with ~50/50 hike odds per CME (a hike would be dollar-positive, metal-negative), and any Section 232 Canada tariff headline. Without a confident directional call I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred at ~$41.9 (tiny negative skew from downside momentum and the likely weaker quarter) with 1-month vol of ~17.5%, i.e. the stock's usual 56%/3.5 = 16% widened slightly for the earnings print.

fair_value.method: Blend of standalone mid-cycle EV/EBITDA ($2.2B 2027E EBITDA x 5.0x less ~$1.45B adjusted net debt = ~$36), skeptic P/E ($4.50 2027E EPS x 9x = $40.5) and consensus P/E ($5.72 x 8x = $45.8), weighted 0.4/0.4/0.2 = ~$40. The South32 AliGroup deal is treated as roughly value-neutral (paid ~9x trough-ish LTM EBITDA with a ticking fee, offset by $50M synergies).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2027E standalone adj. EBITDA $2.2B x 5.0x = EV $11.0B; less adjusted net debt $1.45B; / 264M shares = ~$36

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 run-rate $3.6B was earned at ~$3,400-3,500/t LME and a record Midwest premium. Assume 2027 LME ~$2,950/t (SMM 2027 centre $2,900-3,200; ING/BofA see a 2027 surplus) i.e. ~$450/t below Q2, x ~2.7Mt aluminium shipments (guidance 2.6-2.8Mt) = ~-$1.2B; Midwest premium modestly lower (-$0.1-0.2B); alumina flat near $350-370/t with Pinjarra recovered (+$0.0-0.1B). Net ~$2.2B.

Commodity producers at/after an earnings peak trade at low multiples; current EV (~$11.1B equity + $1.45B net debt) on annualised Q2 EBITDA is ~3.5x, and bear-side writers argue peak margins should not be capitalised. 5x on a normalised (not peak) EBITDA sits mid of Alcoa's historical 4-6x cycle range.

Consensus $5.72 haircut ~21% because consensus has not fully reflected the 2027 surplus (ING, SMM, BofA) and the September price slide; ~$0.5B lower EBITDA than the implied consensus path after tax (~70% flow-through) on 264M shares ~ -$1.2/share.
Cyclical metals stocks earn low multiples on above-mid-cycle earnings; 9x on a haircut (closer to normalised) EPS.
Lower multiple applied to the unhaircut consensus number, as consensus EPS embeds still-elevated metal prices; the stock currently trades at ~7.3x this figure.

bear.story: 2027 surplus arrives as EGA Al Taweelah returns by Q1 2027, Alba/Qatalum normalise and Indonesia ramps to ~2.5Mt; LME drops to ~$2,500-2,600/t, Midwest premium falls on Canada tariff relief, US consumer weakness (confidence 81.9, lowest since 2014) and a Fed hike hit demand. EBITDA ~$1.3-1.5B; AliGroup closes H1 2027 adding $2.6B of 6.6-6.9% notes so leverage moves to ~3x on trough EBITDA; the market prices Alcoa at 4-5x trough EBITDA.

base.story: Aluminium drifts to ~$2,900-3,100/t as the deficit narrows to a small surplus; alumina near $350-380/t; Pinjarra stabilises. EBITDA ~$2.2-2.6B standalone, deal closes and is roughly neutral per share; stock stays around ~5x EBITDA / 8-9x EPS.

bull.story: Gulf restarts slip and Chinese capacity cap binds, LME holds >$3,300/t with thin LME stocks (~240kt); Midwest premium stays >$2,000/t; AliGroup closes and adds earnings at high prices plus synergies; analysts' $60-80 targets get re-validated.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$27 (about 35% under today and below the 52-week low of $31.45) the market would be pricing trough-level aluminium (~$2,500/t) or a balance-sheet problem: post-deal net debt of ~$4.5B with the $2.6B notes is fine at ~2x on today's prices but would approach 3x+ on trough EBITDA. A move there would most likely mean the 2027 surplus thesis has turned into a price collapse, or there is an operational or regulatory failure (WA bauxite approvals, Pinjarra/Worsley), rather than ordinary volatility.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results and call; Q4 outlook; refinery stability and Pinjarra update; deal financing
FOMC decision (CME ~50/50 hike odds); a hike strengthens the dollar and weighs on metals

Decision on cutting the Section 232 tariff on Canadian aluminium from 50% to 25%; lower tariff cost for Alcoa Canada but pressure on the Midwest premium

EGA Al Taweelah targets full restoration, adding Gulf supply back
Closing of the South32 AliGroup acquisition (South32 vote, regulators); ~17M new shares; 5% ticking fee accrues; notes must be redeemed if not closed by 2027-06-29

key_uncertainties: Size and timing of the 2027 aluminium surplus (Gulf restarts, Indonesia ramp, China 45Mt cap)
Midwest premium path under Section 232 changes for Canada and other partners
Alumina price near cost: refinery losses and buying more alumina exposure (Worsley, Alumar) at this point in the cycle
Deal execution and leverage: $2.6B new notes at 6.6-6.9%, ~2.0x pro forma leverage at recent prices that rises at trough prices
US macro: consumer confidence collapse and Fed hike risk vs a supply-driven metals market
WA bauxite approvals and grade decline affecting Pinjarra/Kwinana-style refinery stability
reasoning: Alcoa (AA) at $42 is down 50% from its June 2026 peak of $84.38, when the Hormuz closure took out Gulf smelters and pushed LME to a four-year high of $3,855/t. Since then the market has priced normalisation: a US-Iran deal, EGA targeting full Al Taweelah output by Q1 2027, Chinese and Indonesian supply rising, and ING, BofA and SMM all calling a 2027 surplus (SMM 2027 centre prices $2,900-3,200/t). Q2 results missed (adj. EPS $2.12 vs $2.25-2.32), alumina guidance was cut on Pinjarra instability, and alumina is weak at ~$350-370/t FOB WA. In skeptic terms the main things that could make the Buy/$63 consensus wrong on the downside are: (1) consensus 2027 EPS of $5.72 still assumes elevated metal prices, and each $100/t of LME is worth ~$0.27B a year in EBITDA on ~2.7Mt of shipments; (2) Alcoa is levering up into the cycle, with $2.6B of 6.625%/6.875% notes and pro forma total debt of $5.42B against LTM pro forma EBITDA of $3.07B that is flattered by the Q2 spike, a ticking fee, and Moody's/S&P affirmations that rest on 'recent prices'; (3) the Midwest premium is exposed to Canada tariff relief; (4) WA bauxite approvals and refinery stability are an ongoing regulatory and operational risk; (5) macro is deteriorating (consumer confidence 81.9, Fed hike odds ~50%). Weighed honestly: much of this is already priced. The stock trades at ~3.5x annualised Q2 EBITDA and ~7x consensus 2027 EPS, aluminium is still ~$3,200/t (high by history), LME stocks are thin (~240kt), and sell-side targets are $50-80 with B. Riley and Freedom raising in late September. My blended fair value of ~$40 is slightly below spot, so I centre the 12-month distribution at a median of ~$41 with lognormal sigma ~0.52 (a bit under the 56% realised vol, since the June spike inflated it, but wider than a typical large cap because of commodity beta and deal leverage). Scenario mix (bear $24 / base $42 / bull $65 at 25/50/25) gives a mean of ~$43, consistent with a ~$41 median under right skew. Research limits: Seeking Alpha and Morningstar pages returned 403, Twelve Data analyst and insider endpoints were unavailable on the plan, and the price-sensitivity figure is derived from shipment guidance rather than taken from a company disclosure.
